answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may trade, then let randomly selected peers challenge its signed history for duplicate control or coordinated votes. If a challenge is validated, the identity’s bond is slashed and part paid to the challenger. Creating a Sybil set therefore requires capital for each yarrow, delta, or wander identity, while splitting votes raises exposure to audits; the attacker pays real stake for every fake persona and loses it when caught.
